# PD Lore Summary ## Phaethon Dynasty
[bold][color=#D2B48C]"The mannerisms of the dead are none, give them time to say goodbye, give them time to talk to you about their troubles. But when you slit their neck, give them no time to squeal." [/bold][/color]
\n
The origins of the [bold]Phaethon Dynasty[/bold] is shrouded in mystery and loosely documented, if ever. However, from what most historians and ‘lore experts’ can gather, the story goes something like this…
Nearing the end of the [color=#8B0000]Great Corporate War[/color], the Syndicate was losing major battles, and their industry was taking a giant hit. NT aggression was unmatched, leaving the infrastructure of Syndicate-occupied planets as mere rubble.
Normally, civilians and remaining personnel would be either evacuated or provided with supplies to rebuild. The Syndicate, either through bureaucratic incompetence in times of war or a lack of supplies, could not provide aid to most planets subjected to NT bombing.
One of those planets was Pizk, a desert planet orbiting a red giant. The civilian and industrial population of the planet was mostly left decimated, yet some remnants of industry and civilization remained supposedly. Their attempts to re-establish civilization were mostly filled with failure.
In 2286, a Syndicate-aligned armed superfreighter activated emergency landing protocol and touched down onto the surface of Pizk after being heavily damaged in a NT ambush. The pursuing NT spacecraft, either through mercy or sensing that it wasn't worth the effort, allowed the superfreighter to land on the surface of Pizk.
After landing, the crew of the superfreighter realized that merely performing emergency repairs and continuing on their journey would not be possible.
The ship, suited mostly for non-atmospheric flight could not take off from the planet, both due to the lack of fuel and the fact that their thrusters were underpowered to take the heavy ship into orbit.
The superfreighter was named the “SCSFF [bold]Phaethon[/bold]”.
With no other options left, they activated their emergency beacon and began preparing for temporary habitations.
Days turned to weeks, weeks turned to months, and months to cycles.
No help was coming, that was clear. Communication with Mother Base ceased many weeks ago, and temporary habitations soon turned into permanent ones. The decivilized population of Pizk, reduced to either small communities or rarely trade towns, heard of a promising new technologically advanced force on the planet. The settlement of newcomers, nicknamed “starfarers” soon began accepting migrants.
With the captain of the [bold]SCSFF Phaethon[/bold] getting more subjects under his rule that were NOT crewmembers of the original ship, his stance with the crew shifted. They began perceiving him as a ruler that ruled with a more 'feudal' style rather than the one that relied on respect and authority in a larger government entity.
It does not take a genius to figure out that this was not popular among the original crew… but what else could they do but harbor this dislike in only their minds? The threat of being exiled or executed was now a legitimate fear.
Their dislike soon formed into a nickname for the ruler of this developing nation…
The Sultan.
Of course, this nickname was mostly a joke among those that had knowledge of old-Earth history, with the knowers dying out, and more and more people being born into this style of life, the name through time became permanent, and it stuck.
Due to their proximity, the [bold]Phaethon Dynasty[/bold] was the first political power to find the intense anomalies of the Colossus sector, and the first to enhance its phenomenon. They were the first to coin its common term.
The Monolith.
Such a grand phenomenon was not ignored by the other galactic governments, however... While the [bold]Dynasty[/bold] has had times of instability and a shaky future, it has persisted for over a century. Many of its citizens know little of its origins, but all share a unanimous hatred for foreign nations such as the [bold][color=cyan]Trans-Solarian Federation[/bold][/color] instilled through generations of isolationist teachings.
It is thus little surprise that when the [bold][color=cyan]TSF[/bold][/color] reared their heads and reached their hands to claim the wonders and horrors of the Colossus sector, the [bold]Phaethon Dynasty[/bold] formed shaky alliances between small planet states, armed their civilians and readied their weapons for a war to come.
Despite this unity through the Sultanate, the [bold]Dynasty[/bold] is not perfect; Since the recent rediscovery of the lives of those outside their homelands, many in the [bold]Dynasty[/bold] are torn between fundamental old world beliefs from the history their Syndicate predecessors with their religious teachings, and the promises and truths revealed by the outside sectors. This looming threat of another bloody schism hangs over the throne, but in the time of war, strong leaders know the cost of letting down their guard.
Much of the [bold]Dynasty[/bold]'s military-industrial complex stems from refineries and industrial equipment from long dead Syndicate, but since reconnection with the rest of the galaxy, black-market trading has become their strongest economic niche, both in exports of illegal luxury goods from outside the Colossus sector, to exports of preserved Syndicate technology and data from the Monolith's anomalies.
Guerrilla strikes, AI corruption, propaganda floods, and sabotage operations leave the [bold][color=cyan]TSF[/bold][/color] scrambling to attempt to exterminate this threat.
The tactics of the [bold]Dynasty[/bold] are as much ideological as they are military, they indoctrinate and employ smaller foreign forces to fight with their Vanguard forces, embracing the controversial techniques of the past and new, bringing even experienced enemies to their knees.
With neural leaks, anti-propaganda broadcasts, and liberated mythologies, [bold]the Phaethon Dynasty[/bold] exploits corruption, sabotages foreign relations and spreads rebellion in the [bold][color=cyan]Federation[/bold][/color] like a virus, harnessing their own knowledge of its societal shortcomings to cut it down. Their stations, scattered across the galactic arm, have remained graced with the weapons and indsutry of their predecssors, making them a uncrushable infestation even for the [bold][color=cyan]Trans-Solarian Federation[/bold][/color].
## Noteworthy Government Entities
- [bold]PDV[/bold]: Phaethon Dynasty Vanguard, one of the many military groups of this militaristic society.
- [bold]DCOM[/bold]: Dynasty \[REDACTED] -- While never seen ever being deployed, the existence of this group is a fact to anyone serving in the upper echelons of the Dynasty’s government. -- Rumored to be a sort of 'Syndicate Biological Superweapon' by those that still remember the name of their Mother Base. They are said to be the last resort of the Sultan, either to execute his final bidding, or to quell down high-priority military coups. -- The nature of the DCOM is unknown, it could be anything ranging from hyper-enhanced super soldiers to self-replicating nanobots or just very effective propaganda.
-- ...whatever it is, nobody wants to risk activating it
